additional_info.subject: Question to NOC
additional_info.body:
It appears that COAP is a known issue as identified by Product care.
In the service community discussion, there is discussion about a mitigation process. Has that been applied to this charger?
Can this mitigation be applied to all AU/NZ chargers before it becomes an issue?
Please also understand that the explanation given to the customer was not satisfactory and they have come back directly to me for a clearer explanation.
They do not know what COAP means, they do not know if it can happen again, if it affects their other chargers and when it could happen. We need to be mindful, but all customers are charger expects, we can not just give the answer and then close the ticket, only if the customer is satisfied we have fully answered their questions to the best of our ability should we close the ticket.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0375941-DC/Si-D/NZ-[MP / N5 160345946] Out of order CRM:01811000243
additional_info.body:
Hello Liz,
Thank you for reaching out. We’d like to inform you that the COAP error you’ve encountered is due to a  interruption in internal communication between the SiC D and the SECC. Please rest assured that this is a temporary issue, and the SiC D will automatically reconnect to the SECC within approximately 5 seconds.
During this period when the SECC is unreachable, you may see an "Outlet out of order" flag. This is a normal indication that the system is not currently connected, but this status will be cleared as soon as the connection is reestablished. Additionally, you might notice a "preparing" status displayed in the HM occasionally, which is also part of the normal recovery process.
Thank you.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team - Ankita
